conviction_note: The fiscal Q4 quarter was pre-released on 2026-10-07 (margins at or near the high end of every segment guide, stock +0.08% that day), so the move turns on the first FY27 and Q1 FY27 guide and on oil. US land counterparties that reported after HP last spoke (PTEN, Nabors, Precision) point to more rigs and higher dayrates in Oct-Dec, which is HP's fiscal Q1. Saudi suspensions at the same customer (Aramco) point to a lower International guide. The stock is down about 16% since 28 Oct on a 16% Brent drop. Taken together that is a slight long lean (p_up 54) on a large unsigned move (6.0, first FY guide, ATM IV 115% on a two-day expiry). Findings sum +1.3 against a scaled +0.48. The gap comes from the sign uncertainty, which sits in p_up, and from the oil tape on 19 Nov, which nothing here can see.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-07 HP pre-released fiscal Q4 (Jul-Sep 2026) in an item 2.02 8-K: direct margins in NAS, International and Offshore all at or near the high end of guidance (NAS guide $245-255m, International $25-45m with about $45m expected, Offshore $26-30m). NAS rig count near the high end of 145-151, International near the 60-70 midpoint. So the reported quarter is known, and consensus EPS ($0.26-0.27 at Chartmill/Benzinga) has had six weeks to absorb it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock moved +0.08% on the 2026-10-07 pre-release day (baseline). Q3's +11.4% came on a revenue beat with an adjusted EPS in line/miss, so the reported EPS line has not driven the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: public for six weeks, and the stock did not react. Only a residual remains: whether the actual figures land above the high end (International above $45m) or exactly at it. If the market expected a disappointment, consensus would sit below the high-end-implied run rate, and it does not.

findings.finding: In the same 2026-10-07 8-K the CEO said he expects stronger overall direct margins in fiscal 2027 than fiscal 2026, North America activity staying robust, and Latin America growth partly offset by near-term Middle East reductions. The CFO reaffirmed about 1x net debt/adjusted EBITDA by calendar year-end 2027 with the base dividend kept. The FY27 guide at this print is the first chance to see numbers behind that claim. FY26 NAS direct margin runs about $240-250m a quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last initial-FY guide print (2025-11-17, FY26 guide) fell -3.80% (baseline). The Q3 print with the Q4 guide rose +11.39%.
findings.why_not_priced: The statement is qualitative and public, but the stock has fallen about 16% since 28 Oct as oil dropped. That decline is consistent with the market discounting the FY27 claim for lower oil. If the market fully trusted the claim, the shares would not sit 23% below a mean target set in October. A numeric guide that holds FY27 above FY26 would contradict that discount.
findings.independence: Shares a document with the pre-release finding. Peer US land commentary (PTEN 2026-10-28, https://www.newswire.com/news/patterson-uti-energy-reports-financial-results-for-the-quarter-ended-4618616) independently expects more reactivations in Q1 2027 and higher FCF in 2027.

findings.finding: Saudi land activity at HP's International customer is being cut. Nabors (2026-10-27/28) said SANAD, its Aramco land JV, suspended five rigs in calendar Q4, from 56 to about 52. Patterson-UTI (2026-10-28) guided drilling-products profit down 5-10% on 'lower drilling activity in Saudi Arabia due to ongoing geopolitical unrest'. In August HP said 22 of its rigs work in Saudi Arabia, expected to hold through fiscal Q4 (Jul-Sep), and on 7 Oct it flagged 'near-term Middle East activity reductions'. A Q1 FY27 International guide below the roughly $45m Q4 run rate is likely.
findings.link: Same customer (Saudi Aramco onshore land drilling) and the same product (land rigs). Saudi is about 22 of HP's about 65 International rigs (about one third). International is about $45m of about $330m total Q4 direct margin (about 14%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HP disclosed Saudi suspensions in early 2025 (14 rigs suspended). The Feb 2025 print fell -16.48% (baseline); the cause was not isolated to Saudi. The Nov 2025 print, which carried 7 Saudi reactivations, fell -3.80%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. HP itself flagged Middle East reductions on 7 Oct, and the peer disclosures are three weeks old. What has not been seen is HP's own suspension count and the Q1 International margin number. The Middle East war (ninth month, Houthi attacks on Saudi sites per Reuters via Nation Thailand 2026-11-14) may have added suspensions since the peers spoke. If fully priced, sell-side International estimates would already sit well below $45m, and no such cut was found.
findings.independence: PTEN release, a different source pointing the same way: https://www.newswire.com/news/patterson-uti-energy-reports-financial-results-for-the-quarter-ended-4618616. HP's own 7 Oct 8-K wording on 'near-term Middle East activity reductions'. Sized net of NAS (about 75% of direct margin), which is guided by the US land finding below.

findings.finding: US land counterparties that reported after HP's 7 Oct update guided the Oct-Dec quarter (HP's fiscal Q1 FY27) up. Patterson-UTI: about 104 US rigs average in Q4 (101 in Q3, 92 in Q2), exit above that, 'higher dayrates across all rig classes', more reactivations in Q1 2027. Nabors: Lower 48 to 75 rigs in Q4 from 72.8. Precision Drilling: US operating margins expected up about 30% in Q4. The Baker Hughes oil rig count on 2026-11-13 was 463, +46 year on year, with the Permian at 275.
findings.link: Same US land super-spec rig market and the same E&P customer base. HP's NAS (about 145-151 rigs, about 75% of HP direct margin) is the largest US land fleet. The peers' calendar Q4 is exactly HP's fiscal Q1 FY27, which HP guides at this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NAS guidance prints: Q3 FY26 (NAS margin $241m, Q4 guide $245-255m) rose +11.39%. The Nov 2025 initial FY guide fell -3.80%. 5 of the last 7 prints were negative (baseline), so this name has not reliably paid for good NAS lines.
findings.why_not_priced: The peers spoke three weeks ago, but HP has since fallen about 16% with oil, which reads as the market pricing a 2027 slowdown in E&P budgets. The peers' Q4 guides and Q1 2027 reactivation commentary point to a NAS Q1 guide at or above Q4 and to pricing gains. If that were priced, HP would have tracked the peers' guide-ups rather than oil.
findings.independence: Nabors (https://worldoil.com/news/2026/10/28/nabors-signs-rig-contract-to-return-to-venezuela-as-sanad-deploys-17th-newbuild/), Precision (https://boereport.com/2026/10/27/precision-drilling-announces-2026-third-quarter-unaudited-financial-statements/) and the Baker Hughes count (https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/baker-hughes-rig-count-oil-unch-at-463-natgas--4-at-127-total--3-at-601) are separate documents pointing the same way.

findings.finding: Expectations are reset lower into the print. HP fell from about $41.81 on 2026-10-28 to $35.08 on 2026-11-18 (about -16%; 20-day -8.3%, 5-day -4.2%), while Brent fell 16% and WTI 13% in the week to 2026-11-06 and about 2.5% more to 13 Nov. The drivers were an easing Iran-war risk premium and an IEA surplus warning. Brent still sat at $95.84 and WTI at $88.56 on 13 Nov, well above levels that cut US land budgets. So the bar for a 'FY27 above FY26' guide has fallen with the share price, not with the commodity's level.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Into Q2 FY26 (May 2026) the stock had fallen 3.5% the day before on an oil drop tied to Iran de-escalation, then fell 7.7% more on a revenue and EPS miss (Barchart search snippet, https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1780010/helmerich-payne-hp-stock-trades-down-here-is-why). So an oil-driven drawdown into the print did not protect the stock when the print missed.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown itself is priced by definition. The claim is that it has taken HP below what a supportive guide implies. Oil at about $89-96 is still high, and peers guided up. If the market believed land activity would hold, HP would sit nearer the $45 mean target. Oil's own move on 19 Nov is unknowable and dominates.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew and a negative run-up (-8.3% over 20 days, -4.2% over 5). The slight long lean agrees with the free control (-run_up) and does not cut against any option statement. The main counterweight is this name's habit of falling after prints (5 of 7) and the dominance of the oil tape on the reaction day.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside guided range): the pre-release finding is inside what the company already told the market, so it moved toward 0 (+0.3 -> +0.1).
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): the Saudi/International finding was re-sized net of NAS, about 75% of direct margin, which peers guided up (-1.0 -> -0.7).
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; 5 of the last 7 prints fell): the US land counterparty finding came down (+1.0 -> +0.8), and p_up went 55 -> 54.
Lesson 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a proxy): the oil/expectations finding came down (+0.8 -> +0.5). It was kept because the drawdown has a sourced cause (oil), not an absence of one.

Lesson 7: short interest was checked before the negative Saudi finding; not crowded, so no shrink on that ground. Lesson 8 does not apply (well covered, no unpriced company-level number). abs_move_pct stays at 6.0 because this is a first-FY-guide print.
